blocks.text: NEW YORK — Thanksgiving storms brought foul weather to the East Coast and other parts of the US on Thursday, causing coastal and power outages and prompting the postponement of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. High winds and flooding hammered both coasts, snarling holiday travel. More than 800,000 homes and businesses were without electricity Thursday afternoon, with the majority of outages in East Coast states, according to the outage tracking website poweroutage.us. By midday Thursday, 1,700 flights to or from U.S. destinations were delayed and more than 400 were cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.
